newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nail plans rights issue, up Metlife stake.
newsitem.headline: Nail plans rights issue, up Metlife stake.

text.p: New Africa Investments Ltd said on Wednesday it plans to hold a rights issue to raise one billion rand and proposes to increase its stake in Metropolitan Life Ltd to 34.9 percent.
Nail said in a statement the rights offer would be in the form of N-shares.
"(The issue will) partly fund the Metlife acquisition, fund the AMB capitalisation, repay short-term debt, fund current obligations and to take advantage of future growth opportunities," Nail said.
Nail announced at the same time that it planned to list AMB (African Merchant Bank), in which Nail holding firm Nafhold holds a 27.5 percent stake, on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in due course.
It said AMB had experienced phenomenal growth since its inception and would be capitalised further to position it as a merchant banking group with a capital base of 500 million rand.

This would give AMB critical mass and it would be able to exploit synergies in co-operation with Metlife. A separate listing would also ensure that the bank's underlying value was fully reflected in the Nail share price.

Nail said further that the additional Metlife acquisition -- Nafhold currently holds a 29.3 percent stake in Metlife -- would not have an immediate effect on its earnings or net asset value but would end the voting pool arrangement with Sankorp, a shareholder of Metlife.

Nail earlier reported a 37.2 percent jump in interim earnings per share 3.69 cents. Directors decided not to declare a dividend as the firm was expanding its capital base by means of the one billion rand rights issue.
The proposed listing of Nafhold, Nail's financial services holding company, would not proceed as had been proposed, Nail said. Accordingly the Nafhold minority would be made an offer for its shares.
The company published cautioneries on April 3, 24 and June 3 saying talks were in progress between itself, Metlife, Nafhold and Sankorp and gave no further details.
